lines.t: Hi! I'm Mo. I build things around town. Today I'm building Amy's counter.
But the Smudge blew my 3 planks all over the market. Each one is 1 m 65 cm long.
Look for anything that sparkles, {name}. Walk right onto it to pick it up.
All 3 planks! Thank you, {name}.
Each one is 1 m 65 cm. Laid end to end, how long will Amy's counter be?
Work it out on the Two-Unit Mat on the Learn tab. Then come back and tell me.
Type the length in centimeters, then press OK.
495 cm! That's 4 m 95 cm. Same as on your mat.
Stand back. Counter time!
You built the counter on the mat? Then you're just the helper I need.
My saw only shows centimeters.
How many centimeters long is the whole counter?
That counter came out just right. 4 m 95 cm, measured twice!
I'm Mo. I build things around town. Wood comes in meters and centimeters, but my saw reads only centimeters. Tricky!

lines.t: Hoo! You made it, {name}! Today is Market Day in Metric Market.
I'm Opti. I'll travel with you and the Math Crew all year.
Amy wants to open her juice stand today. But last night the Smudge rolled through town.
The Smudge is a grumpy gray cloud. It mixed up every measure in town.
Mo is building Amy's counter, Millie is bringing flour, and Amy has juice orders to fill. The Market Day board on the page lists every job.
Let's start here. Walk over to the Liter Well and read its sign. Tell me if it looks right.
The Liter Well is east of the fountain. Look for the stone well with the little red roof.
Listen to that line at Amy's stand! Nice work, {name}.
Hoo! Every job on the Market Day board gets Amy one step closer to opening.
(calling from the platform) Keep that question in your pocket, {name}. By the end of this lesson, you'll prove the answer.
You proved it, {name}. 1 L is 1,000 mL, so 2 L is 2,000 mL. Not 200!
Rest up. Next lesson we cross the Foot Bridge, where people measure in inches and feet.

lines.t: Careful! 6 kg is 6,000 g, not 60 g or 600 g. Then add the 5 g. The zeros hold the places.
Regroup first. 195 cm is 1 m 95 cm. So 3 m 195 cm is 4 m 95 cm. How many centimeters is that?
That's what the Smudge wrote! 1 L = 1,000 mL, not 100 mL. So what is 2 L?
Hello, I'm Cora. I like every word to be exact. That sign on the Liter Well looks wrong to me.
When the centimeters reach 100, trade them for 1 m. That's regrouping!
